To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the TD model with temporal generalization is a good model of classical conditioning, (2) the degree of generalization is a key parameter that influences the performance of a TD model, (3) the degree of temporal generalizaion is not a fixed property of the stimuli but rather a property of the organism's perceptual representation of the stimulus, (4) the degree of stimulus generalization is not fixed and may vary across individuals, across species, and within an individual across tasks

The performance of the TD algorithm is highly dependent on the stimulus representation used in the model and that the TD model is capable of reproducing the key behavioral phenomena of classical conditioning.

(1) The temporal-difference algorithm from reinforcement learning is a simple and powerful method for modeling classical conditioning; (2) The TD algorithm is sensitive to the representation of the conditioned stimulus; (3) The performance of the TD algorithm is comparable to that of other error-correction algorithms, such as Rescorla-Wagner; and (4) The TD algorithm provides an intuitive explanation for the effects of stimulus intensity and temporal contiguity on the learning of a conditioned response.

the performance of the simple TD model with temporal-generalization representations is comparable to the performance of the Rescorla-Wagner model, a widely used model in classical conditioning.

, although the TD model is capable of accounting for the data from a wide range of tasks, its performance can be significantly improved by using a stimulus representation with a greater degree of temporal generalizability.

the TD model can account for a broad range of conditioning phenomena, including the acquisition of a simple CS-US association and the extinction and spontaneous recovery of an association that has already formed, as long as the CS representation has a sufficient degree of temporal generalizability.

the representation of a stimulus in a TD model is a critical determinant of the model's performance on conditioning tasks.
